labels.note: A segment ending in a bare '#' (e.g. "b#") now overwrites the base hash with '#', dropping the base fragment.
The segment's hash never replaces the base hash, so resolveURL loses the requested fragment.
Only reached when the merged query is empty, e.g. both searches are '?&'. Unrealistic input.
If the base has no query, the segment's query is silently dropped. This is a common resolveURL case.
Unreachable: an empty hash already returns early through the !hash guard.
Every protocol is flagged as a script protocol. Security check breaks, e.g. 'https:' returns true.
Any non-empty protocol returns true, so safe protocols are misclassified. Security-relevant.
Inputs like '#x' or '?a' gain a leading '/' (e.g. '/#x' instead of '#x'). Other inputs are rebuilt unchanged.
